summary: Written by: Alex Tselevich, Michael Maturi Introduction Adversarial misuse of AI has increased the risk of data theft and extortion events, because when proprietary source code is exposed, defenders must scramble to identify and patch vulnerabilities while attackers deploy machine-speed AI tools against them. By structuring the analysis process, enforcing skeptical validation steps, and injecting domain-specific human expertise directly into the pipeline, we’ve achieved a leap in efficacy. Combining AI models with a deeply structured, human expert-driven orchestration layer to tip the scales so that defenders can beat adversaries to the punch. Today, we use the Agentic Vulnerability Discovery Harness (AVDH) to rapidly analyze code and find exploit paths during proactive reviews, penetration tests, red team operations, and incident response engagements. By combining multi-agent orchestration with our frontline subject-matter expertise, this framework helps to augment the discovery and validation of routine vulnerabilities, enabling humans to focus their impact. To help defenders implement similar approaches for their own environments, we are sharing the details of this internal, point-in-time architecture for the first time. AVDH can also be used alongside CodeMender’s ongoing scanning to create a two-layered defense strategy. title: Staying Ahead of Adversarial AI Through Agentic Source Code Review

UNC7005 in particular is tied to the hospitality captive portal redirects reported on by Reliaquest and Microsoft . While each group conducts their campaigns differently, they all ultimately demonstrate a focus on abuse of legitimate authentication workflows to compromise accounts. From 0.29.13 until 0.31.0, the Docker terminal, container-log, and monitoring WebSocket handlers accept a caller-controlled serviceId as authorization but do not consistently bind the requested containerId or appName to that service. A member with read access to any service can consequently target unrelated containers, obtain a root shell in the Dokploy panel container, read other tenants' logs and statistics, and use the mounted Docker socket to compromise the host. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.0.
title: CVE-2026-129316 (CVSS 9.9)

summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). Prior to 0.31.1, mount.deleteFileMount passes a path containing the user-controlled filePath to the local removeFileOrDirectory helper, which interpolates it unquoted into rm -rf, while the remote branch is quoted. An authenticated member with file-mount create and delete permissions can execute arbitrary commands in the host context immediately when deleting a local file mount, without requiring a running container. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.
title: CVE-2026-129986 (CVSS 9.9)

This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.
title: CVE-2026-129989 (CVSS 9.9)

summary: Dokploy is a free, self-hostable Platform as a Service (PaaS). An authenticated organization member with backup permission for a service can execute arbitrary commands as root on the Dokploy host or configured remote server when a PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, libSQL, Compose, or web-server backup runs manually, on schedule, or performs retention cleanup. This issue is fixed in version 0.31.1.
